purchases.title: Bitbrand: Bitcoin Saved My Life
purchases.summary:
Bitbrand makes hand-branded Bitcoin goods the old way: steel, fire, and leather. No ink, no printer, and no two pieces alike. He invented the Bitcoin branding iron, calls himself the branding iron broker, and built the company from the back of a van.
In this episode of Share Your Bitcoin Journey, Bitcoin For The Arts founder Dion Wilson meets Bitbrand in Jersey City, after they first met at the Midwest Bitcoin Summit in Columbus. Bitbrand tells how Bitcoin saved his life, how an ATM on the Upper East Side changed what he did with his money, and how he got sober at 30 and quit the corporate job

What Jekyll Island actually was, what it wasn't, and who ended up holding the machine.

purchases.title: Institutions — 21 Essays on Trust and Its Architecture
purchases.summary: Twenty-five minutes. Twenty-one essays. The question underneath all of them: what happens to institutions when trust migrates to protocols? Bitcoin, Ottoman history, Girard, Banfield — the whole radius-of-trust argument in audio form.

purchases.title: The Artifacts of a Life
purchases.summary: The biographical essays are where the intellectual framework becomes flesh. A 256MB JumpDrive becomes a meditation on SHA-256. A Grameen Bank cost-benefit analysis becomes a reckoning with Banfield's radius of trust. Standing in the rubble of Antakya six days after the earthquake. The Joe Wendel funeral essay using 'proof of work' as a metaphor for what you build invisibly over time.

purchases.title: How Good People Drift into Disaster
purchases.summary: The smallest cluster and the sharpest. Six essays using popular culture the way a theologian uses a parable. Girard's mimetic desire runs beneath every system. 'The Choices We Call Necessity' — the Devil Wears Prada essay — is the sharpest piece in the corpus: Hannah Arendt meets Miranda Priestly, and the argument is that moral drift doesn't announce itself. You just stop noticing what you're becoming.

purchases.title: A Lodging of Wayfaring Men
purchases.summary:
This novel was a major influence: first in the Cyber-underground and then in the larger world. "A Lodging of Wayfaring Men" is the story of ethical people who create an alternative society on the Internet – a virtual society, with no possibility of oversight or control. It grows so fast that governments and "leaders" are terrified, and fight to destroy it before it undermines the power of the ruling elite.
